target_customer: Mobile gamers, monetized through in-app purchases
problem: Building and running free-to-play mobile games with collectible creature mechanics at a time when mobile social gaming was growing fast.
business_model: Free-to-play mobile games with in-app purchases

founders.name: Josh Buckley
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is an early investor in many companies.

founders.name: Sash MacKinnon
founders.background_notes: One source says the studio team came from Zynga, Kabam, Sega and Hasbro; not tied to individual founders.

competitors.name: Zynga
competitors.what: Social games leader moving into mobile
competitors.traction_then: Two thirds of 12 games launched in 2011 were mobile

competitors.name: Kabam
competitors.what: Mid-core social and mobile strategy games
competitors.traction_then: Described as leader in emerging mid-core space

competitors.name: Backflip Studios
competitors.traction_then: Cited at GDC Online 2011 as executing mobile strategy well

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard mobile game engineering across iOS and Android, with live operations and monetization tuning as the hard parts for a small studio.

defensibility.rationale: Games are copyable and hits are volatile; durable advantage rests on content and live ops skill rather than structural barriers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an acquisition; the studio stayed independent and later raised for a Web3 game.

market_need_then: Mobile and social gaming was booming in 2011 with record funding of $807M for social games, indicating strong demand and investor appetite.

branding.domain_note: Game site minomonsters.com now redirects to a WordPress blog (minogamesonline.wordpress.com).

identity.mascot_or_character: Collectible pet monsters in the Mino Monsters franchise

branding.community_and_virality: One undated snippet mentions community backlash around an NFT project tied to Mino Games; not verified.

brand_strength.rationale: Studio and game franchise show up in game directories but no press about the brand itself was found.

pivots.from: Mobile games such as Mino Monsters
pivots.why: Not stated in the sources reviewed beyond the funding announcement.

outcome_analysis: Mino Games survived more than a decade as an independent studio, with the YC page claiming a top-25 grossing mobile studio and a16z backing across 2011, 2015 and 2023 rounds. It raised $15M in February 2023 for a Web3 game, a riskier direction; outcomes after that are not found in sources, so the final result is unresolved.
notes: Funding totals conflict (CB Insights shows about $49.7M over 9 rounds); only rounds confirmed by trade press are recorded. Seed 2011 amount unknown. Sources disagree on HQ (San Francisco on YC page, Montreal elsewhere). Top-25 grossing claim is company reported. Competitors are dated 2011 industry context, not product specific comparisons.
